newsitem.title: USA: Harriman's body returned to Washington.
newsitem.headline: Harriman's body returned to Washington.

text.p: The body of U.S. Ambassador to France Pamela Harriman was returned to Washington on Saturday from Paris, where she died Wednesday of a brain hemmorage at the age of 76.

"Today we are here to welcome home a great American. She served her country with skill, grace, eloquence and elegance," Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said at a ceremony at Andrews Air Force Base, Maryland, after Harriman's coffin arrived on a U.S. Air Force jet.

"Nobody loved this country more or cherished American values more than Pamela Harriman. How well she represented us all. She was a master of the personal touch," Albright added. She returned from a trip to Houston in time for the ceremony.
The coffin was carried off the jet by a U.S. military honour guard and Harriman received a 15-gun salute. A military band played hymns and the U.S. national anthem.
Harriman's son, Winston Spencer Churchill, a British member of parliament, said he and his family were grateful for the honours given to his mother, a naturalised U.S. citizen.
"She fought tenatiously for the interests of her adopted country and of the western alliance," Churchill said.
About 100 people including government officials and family members were present at the ceremony, held inside a hanger because of a heavy snowfall.
Earlier in Paris, French President Jacques Chirac came to the U.S. Embassy and placed the red sash of the Grand Cross of the French Legion of Honour on Harriman's coffin.
He told her a month ago that he planned to give her France's highest award. "It is my great regret that the ceremony has become a last leave-taking," Chirac said.

"To say that she was an exceptional representative of the United States in France does not do justice to her achievement: she lent to our longstanding alliance the radiant strength of her personality. She was elegance itself. She was grace," Chirac added.

Harriman will be buried this Friday at Arden House in New York state, former residence of her husband, the late New York governor and U.S. diplomat, Averell Harriman, after services in Washington on Thursday where President Bill Clinton will give the eulogy.
